purpose: Test whether the linear-size GF(3) syndrome in v5.5 can be compressed by quotienting out a large formula-dependent subspace that contains no attainable nonzero syndrome. Characterize exactly when such a quotient is zero-reflecting and identify the optimal-kernel search as the classical Critical Problem of Crapo-Rota, which already generalizes graph colouring. Freeze finite graphic controls showing that substantial safe kernels can exist but their geometry varies sharply with the instance.

setup.cycle_matrix: Let Q be a beta by m full-row-rank GF(3) cycle matrix of a connected graph.
setup.attainable_syndromes: S(Q)={Q s : s in Sigma} subset GF(3)^beta.
setup.original_zero_test: A nowhere-zero tension / proper 3-colouring exists iff 0 belongs to S(Q).
setup.linear_quotient: Let H:GF(3)^beta -> GF(3)^k be linear with kernel D. The compressed test asks whether 0 belongs to H(S(Q)), equivalently whether S(Q) intersects D.

theorem.name: ZERO_REFLECTING_LINEAR_SYNDROME_QUOTIENT_IFF_KERNEL_AVOIDS_ATTAINABLE_NONZERO_SYNDROMES
theorem.statement: Every compressed zero witness lifts to a genuine zero syndrome iff D intersect (S(Q)-{0}) is empty.
proof: H(Qs)=0 iff Qs lies in ker(H)=D.
If D contains an attainable nonzero syndrome y=Qs, then the quotient accepts s although Qs is not zero, so zero reflection fails.

Conversely, if D contains no attainable nonzero syndrome, every attainable syndrome killed by H is zero; therefore any quotient-zero sign assignment is already a genuine tension and reconstructs a 3-colouring exactly.
theorem.compression_dimension: Among strong zero-reflecting linear quotients, maximum removable syndrome dimension is max dim(D) over linear subspaces D with D intersect S*(Q)=empty, where S*(Q)=S(Q)-{0}.

critical_problem_identification.classical_definition: For a subset S of GF(q)^k-{0}, the Critical Problem asks for the maximum dimension of a linear subspace D disjoint from S; the critical exponent/number is the complementary codimension.
critical_problem_identification.identity: Therefore optimal strong linear syndrome compression for S*(Q) is exactly one instance of the Critical Problem, after identifying scalar-multiple syndrome vectors projectively.
critical_problem_identification.firewall: The Critical Problem is a classical matroid problem that includes graph colouring as a special case. Hence the instruction 'find the largest syndrome-avoiding kernel' is not itself a licensed polynomial step; it merely moves the hard combinatorics into the kernel-construction problem.
critical_problem_identification.implicit_input_warning: Here S*(Q) is not even supplied explicitly: it is the image of an exponential sign cube. Materializing all attainable syndromes before solving the Critical Problem is forbidden.

bad_c8_two_c4.graph: Hamiltonian C8 with complementary C4s [0,3,1,6] and [2,4,7,5], the frozen v5.3 non-3-colourable control.

safe_kernel.fact: All 3^4=81 vectors in this subspace are absent from S(Q), so quotienting beta=9 down to k=5 is zero-reflecting on this control.

good_c8_two_c4.graph: Hamiltonian C8 with complementary C4s [0,3,1,5] and [2,6,4,7], the frozen colourable control.
good_c8_two_c4.strong_kernel_control: After removing the genuine zero syndrome from S(Q), the complement contains 523 projective points but no complete projective line. Equivalently there is no two-dimensional strong zero-reflecting kernel; the maximum strong safe-kernel dimension is one. The checker verifies all projective pairs exactly.

finite_graphic_controls.meaning: Large safe kernels can occur, but their existence and dimension are highly instance-sensitive. The finite controls do not imply a SAT criterion; they are regression tests for any proposed source-computable kernel rule.

positive: Linear syndrome quotienting is fully characterized: a candidate kernel can be verified exactly against an explicit finite control and, if source theory proves avoidance, gives immediate dimension reduction with exact witness lifting.

The bad control demonstrates that substantial graphic compression is algebraically possible in principle; the v1.9 generic all-nonzero-syndrome obstruction does not automatically occur on every graphic instance.
killed: Treat maximum syndrome-avoiding-subspace search as a free polynomial compression primitive.
Choose an arbitrary low-dimensional linear hash and infer exactness without proving that its kernel avoids every attainable nonzero syndrome.
Materialize S(Q) or the projective Critical-Problem instance exponentially and count that as polynomial.
not_killed: A graph-structural rule that constructs a large safe kernel directly from Hamiltonian/interlacement data and proves avoidance without solving the implicit Critical Problem generically.
An iterative contraction where each safe kernel vector is certified by a polynomial graphic obstruction.
Nonlinear syndrome compression or a nonalgebraic minimax invariant with exact reconstruction.

next_target.name: E8_SOURCE_CERTIFIED_SAFE_KERNEL_OR_INTERLACEMENT_CONTRACTION_V5_7
next_target.directive: Do not optimize over the implicit syndrome set. Seek polynomially checkable sufficient conditions, stated directly in the Hamiltonian/C4 interlacement graph or cycle matrix Q, that certify one or more independent kernel directions as unattainable. Each successful contraction must strictly reduce beta, preserve zero reflection, and reconstruct a sign basis. If no such local/source certificate exists, produce a finite family showing why the certificate class is incomplete.

sources: Crapo and Rota, On the Foundations of Combinatorial Theory: Combinatorial Geometries, 1970 (Critical Problem).
Critical Problem for a q-analogue of polymatroids, Discrete Mathematics, 2024/2025, for the modern formulation and relation of critical exponent to graph colouring.
